take_homes: The context I give the model decides what comes back. The first answer in a conversation shapes every later one.
The agent grades its own work too kindly. Treat its report as a hypothesis and check it against what I saw, or use a fresh reader with no history.
What I learn can be saved as a rules file that the next session reads, so the work does not start from scratch.

monday.move: Run the LinkedIn exercise once, perhaps 20 minutes, to see whether the baseline-versus-context difference is real. Nothing else.
monday.when: Tuesday or Wednesday, between steering groups
monday.stop_condition: If the output with context is not clearly better than the baseline, I stop and file this with the other programmes.
monday.blocker: The calendar and the steering groups. Also, I have not asked IT about connectors and customer data.

misconception.why: I had the 'wait and see, it will blow over' view. The module did not prove otherwise, but it was candid that the tool flatters its own work, and I can test that myself. That is the first thing here that the last three programmes never offered. I still read about a dozen generic paragraphs that sounded exactly like them.

one_line: There are two or three honest, useful ideas here, like the tool marking its own homework too kindly, but they sit between a dozen paragraphs of the same transformation text I have seen three times.
